## Step-by-step solution

**Given:**
- Prevalence: P(Disease) = 1/500 = 0.002, so P(No Disease) = 0.998
- Sensitivity: P(Positive | Disease) = 0.98
- Specificity: P(Negative | No Disease) = 0.95, so P(Positive | No Disease) = 0.05

**Apply Bayes' theorem:**

$$P(\text{Disease}\mid\text{Positive}) = \frac{P(\text{Positive}\mid\text{Disease})\,P(\text{Disease})}{P(\text{Positive}\mid\text{Disease})\,P(\text{Disease}) + P(\text{Positive}\mid\text{No Disease})\,P(\text{No Disease})}$$

**Numerator:**
$$0.98 \times 0.002 = 0.00196$$

**Denominator (total probability of testing positive):**
$$0.00196 + (0.05 \times 0.998) = 0.00196 + 0.0499 = 0.05186$$

**Result:**
$$P(\text{Disease}\mid\text{Positive}) = \frac{0.00196}{0.05186} \approx 0.0377941$$

Converting to a percentage: **3.77941...% ≈ 3.78%**

This illustrates the classic base-rate effect: even with a fairly accurate test (98% sensitivity, 95% specificity), because the condition is rare (0.2% prevalence), most positive results are still false positives — only about 1 in 26 people who test positive actually have the condition.

FINAL ANSWER: 3.78
